_comment: UPRISING — the facts the announcement is built from.
Single source of truth for everything the posts advertise, the same way
blackout-season.json is for Vol.8. The FORMAT numbers are NOT in here: they
are read out of uprising-engine.js by ops/uprising-facts.mjs, so a post can
never advertise a court count, a round count or a points table that the app
contradicts. Only the things the engine cannot know — when, how much, what
you win — live here.
DATE. Saturday 10 Oct — tomorrow, announced the night before. One day to
fill 16 places is the risk the owner chose to take; the post leans on it
rather than hiding it, which is why the date block reads TOMORROW while
that is true. Change `date` and everything re-renders, including that.
PRIZES. ONE prize for the first night: the champion takes a 15 OMR voucher
and nothing else is advertised (see secondPrize below). championPrizeKind
prints 'voucher' under the figure on every card and inside the sentence in
every message — 'champion takes 15 OMR' reads as cash, and somebody turning
up expecting notes would have been misled by our own poster.
The second prize is kept here, switched off: THE CLIMB — most points above
your own average — takes a free entry rather than cash, which costs 7 OMR
of foregone entry instead of 15 in vouchers and brings the winner back next
month. Measured over 200 simulated seasons, a scratch prize alone sends 70%
of nights to the top three players and the handicap 21%, so it is worth
turning back on once there is history to compute it from.
CADENCE LINE. Keep it vague enough to be true: the first post said "first
Saturday night of the month" while advertising the 17th, which is the
third. Nobody will check the maths on "one Saturday a month"; everybody
notices a date that contradicts the line above it.
name: UPRISING
climbPrize: A free entry to the next UPRISING
_secondPrize: FALSE = one prize only. The champion takes the voucher and nothing else
is advertised. Set by the owner for the first night: a second prize that
has to be explained is a second thing that can go wrong on a night nobody
has played before, and the entry fee is the only other number on the card.
The engine still computes upPrizes() — the stress harness asserts on it —
but nothing in the app or the posts reads it while this is false. Set it
true (and firstNight false, once there is history) to put THE CLIMB back,
and every card and caption re-renders with the second block.
_firstNight: THE CLIMB is 'most points per round above your own average', and on the
very first night nobody has an average — every baseline falls back to the
field average, which is the same number for everyone, so the rule collapses
into 'most points' and awards the champion both prizes. Measured: 2000 of
So while firstNight is true the second prize is the STRONGEST FINISH —
most points in the second half of the night minus the first. It needs no
history, it is the champion only 7% of the time, and unlike 'biggest rise
up the ladder' it is not inverted (that one goes 80% to whoever the shuffle
dropped to Court 4 and can never be won from Court 1).
Set this to false after the first night and the posts switch to THE CLIMB.
_courts: How many courts the club actually has on the night. NOT a rule of the
format — the ladder, the points table and the climb all live in
uprising-engine.js. This is the one number the engine cannot know, and
everything downstream reads it through ops/uprising-facts.mjs: the cards,
the captions, the sign-up list, the link preview and the app's home page.
It changes more than the ladder's height. With 16 players on 3 courts, 4
rest every round, which means: 9 matches each instead of 15, a 130-minute
night instead of 150, and NO double final — whoever is resting the last
round could not win it, so the engine switches the doubling off. Anything
advertising 'last round counts double' has to disappear with it, which is
why that line is conditional on facts.doubleFinal everywhere rather than
typed into nine files of copy.
